title: Handling a Difficult Client
paragraphs: One client had developed a habit of sending angry emails over minor delays, and Dina found herself dreading every message that arrived from his particular email address each week.
Rather than responding defensively, she scheduled a phone call to discuss his concerns directly, choosing to listen fully before explaining the reasons behind the recent delays affecting his project.
During the call, the client's tone gradually softened once he realized Dina was genuinely engaging with his frustrations rather than simply offering scripted, generic apologies over email.

Over the following months, their working relationship noticeably improved, and Dina realized that most frustrated clients simply wanted to feel heard rather than receiving perfect solutions immediately.
